flags: cos(theta*) endpoints adjusted from exact +/-1.0 to +/-0.999: the EXCLURAD integrator fails at the exact poles (a known quirk of this channel), so the requested 5-step scan from -1 to +1 was mapped to [-0.999, -0.5, 0.0, 0.5, 0.999] to keep the endpoints physically evaluable while preserving the requested even 5-point spacing over the range.

beam energy defaulted to 6.53 GeV (CLAS12 RG-K, the campaign the validated eta reference data came from); this was not specified in the request. Other CLAS12 energies (10.6, 10.2 GeV) are valid and give different radiative corrections.
rc_mode used = 0 (full O(alpha)), matching every validated eta result; this was not specified in the request.
vcut used = 0.166 GeV^2 (channel default for eta).
explanation: Preflight check on all 5 kinematic points at W=1.7 GeV, Q2=1.5 GeV^2, phi*=90 deg for the eta channel returned PASS for every point (W is safely above the eta+p threshold of 1.4861 GeV, Q2 and phi are within table coverage, beam-energy accessibility is fine at the default 6.53 GeV). The only correction applied was clamping the two scan endpoints from cos(theta*) = -1.0 and +1.0 to -0.999 and +0.999, since the Fortran integrator is documented to fail exactly at the poles; this is a standard, inert fix that does not change the physics content of the scan. The single input file was generated and validated; it is ready to run with EXCLURAD in full O(alpha) mode.
